speaker: Doctor
text: I see you've mentioned a skin condition, but I need to understand your specific symptoms first. Can you describe the appearance of any lesions, including their size, color, and whether they are changing over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the combination of a non-healing lesion on the penis and a similar one on the finger, especially given your age and smoking history, raises concern for malignancy. Have you noticed any bleeding, pain, or recent changes in the size or shape of these spots? REQUEST TEST: CBC, HbA1c, HIV, and Syphilis serology. REQUEST IMAGES: Clinical photos of the penile and digital lesions.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: NORMAL READINGS, HbA1c: NORMAL READINGS, HIV: Negative, Syphilis serology: Negative. Clinical images: Erythematous plaque with areas of crusting and irregular borders on the dorsal penile shaft and left middle finger. Biopsy: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures are highly concerning for a malignancy, likely squamous cell carcinoma given the location and your history. Have you experienced any bone pain, weight loss, or night sweats recently that might suggest metastasis? REQUEST TEST: CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma (penile and digital) with no evidence of distant metastasis. Given the multifocal nature and your history, I need to rule out an underlying genetic predisposition like Xeroderma Pigmentosum or a field cancerization effect. Have you had a history of severe sunburns in childhood, or do you have any other skin cancers on your body?
